title: Grateful Dead Live at Springer's Inn Portland on 1970-01-16
source: Source: sbd > reel master > reel > pcm (sony beta tape ESX-HiFi/L-750) - Given to Tim Dalton by the late Harvey Lubar; Transfer: pcm > Sony SL-10 > Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000 (WAV 16-bit/44.1k) - transferred by Charlie Miller; Lineage: wav > iZotope RX6 Advanced > iZotope 5 Advanced > CD Wave > TLH > Flac 16; edited and mastered SIRMick February 2018

ai_review.summary: Good soundboard capture of a rough early‑70 performance highlighted by a primo China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider segue.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard tape that, while a bit raw as many early‑70 shows are, sounds clear enough to enjoy. The show shines with Jerry’s enthusiastic “China Cat Sunflower > Rider” transition and the overall vibe of this prime Dead era. Reviewers are uniformly positive despite noting the typical roughness of the period.

ai_rating.rationale: Three detailed, mostly 4‑5 star reviews praise the performance and note only minor roughness; recording is a soundboard with decent clarity, yielding an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Rough, early‑70 rawness noted but generally clear; no major dropouts or balance issues reported.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑70 energy with a solid flow; the China>Rider segue is highlighted as a high point, and the show feels “primo Dead” despite its rough edges.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as digging the new China>Rider thing, showing enthusiastic playing.
